response_change.parent_relation: For fixed c0 and p_trigger, c_eff is piecewise constant in p: equal to c0 below threshold and to c0*(1-rho) at and above threshold.
response_change.child_relation: For fixed c0 and p_trigger, contact suppression remains absent below threshold but increases progressively with exceedance above p_trigger, so c_eff decreases smoothly from c0 toward stronger suppression as p rises above the trigger instead of making one fixed drop.
response_change.observable_effect: Holding c0, p_trigger, and rho fixed, two prevalences both above the trigger give the same c_eff under the parent but different c_eff under the child, with lower contact rate at the higher prevalence.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when sampled conditions include p both just above and well above p_trigger with 0<rho<1 and p_trigger>0, so exceedance magnitude varies within the active regime.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, contrast appears between near-threshold and farther-above-threshold active cases; in holdout, the same graded active response extends to broader relative exceedance without changing the inactive-below-threshold branch.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the graded strengthening saturates immediately upon activation, collapsing the active branch back to a fixed suppression fraction rho.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes that once prevalence crosses the trigger, the intervention always removes exactly the same fraction of contacts regardless of whether prevalence barely exceeds or greatly exceeds the threshold.
plan.baseline_assumption: Compliance is constant whenever the intervention is active.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Risk-responsive tightening or intensification of adherence above the trigger, yielding graded suppression strength within the active regime rather than a single fixed active level.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the fixed active suppression assumption while keeping the same inputs and static setting. The parent target mapping has a single active gain: with c0, p_trigger, and rho held fixed, varying p only determines whether the intervention is off or on, and all p>=p_trigger collapse to one c_eff value. The child would instead make suppression strength depend on how far prevalence exceeds the trigger, so the slope with respect to p changes from zero on the active branch to negative, introducing active-branch curvature or graded decline. This is scientifically admissible when measured prevalence spans values just above and substantially above the policy trigger; in that regime, programs often intensify distancing, enforcement, or voluntary compliance as perceived risk rises, even if activation began at one threshold. The target mapping itself changes, not merely an auxiliary trajectory, because the scored c_eff differs for different above-trigger p values under identical c0, p_trigger, and rho. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce this contrast across active cases: changing rho only changes one common active plateau, and changing p_trigger only relocates the jump, but the parent cannot make c_eff distinguish among multiple p values once they are all above threshold. Limitation: if admissible data contain only below-threshold points or only a very narrow band right at activation, the refinement would be weakly observable.

plan.baseline_assumption: Compliance intensification above the trigger follows a single exponential in relative prevalence excess with no additional shape flexibility.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Behavioral and programmatic tightening often ramps up slowly immediately after activation but strengthens more sharply once prevalence is clearly above the trigger, giving a sigmoidal or higher-order saturating active-regime response rather than a single-scale exponential.

The parent target mapping has a single-threshold shortcut: once p exceeds p_trigger, all dependence on prevalence excess is governed by one fixed exponential curvature. Vary p while holding c0, rho, and p_trigger fixed. In the parent, the suppression increment between slight exceedance and moderate exceedance is rigidly tied to the increment between moderate and large exceedance by that one shared shape. In the child, the same threshold remains, but the active branch acquires different curvature, so suppression can remain modest just above threshold yet increase more abruptly at moderate exceedance before saturating below c0. This is a genuine change in the scored mapping c_eff(p,c0,p_trigger,rho), not merely an auxiliary interpretation. The contrast is scientifically admissible when prevalence samples include both near-trigger and clearly above-trigger conditions and rho is neither 0 nor 1. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot generally absorb this across those conditions because changing p_trigger shifts onset and changing rho rescales amplitude, but neither creates an independently sharper mid-range bend while preserving the same threshold and asymptote.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when prevalence samples lie in a neighborhood of the trigger, with |p-p_trigger|/p_trigger not large; away from the trigger both parent and child approach the same inactive or saturated-active behavior.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: Training can see ordinary above-trigger tightening, while holdout can emphasize dense sampling near the trigger; the same mechanism appears in both, but only near-threshold conditions reveal the rounded onset absent from the parent.
plan.continuation_path: In the limit of vanishing measurement/decision smoothing width, the rounded activation recovers the parent Heaviside-triggered law.
plan.gap_statement: The current law assumes exact, instantaneous threshold recognition, producing an unrealistically sharp activation boundary in the scored mapping from measured prevalence to controlled contact rate.
plan.baseline_assumption: The intervention activates immediately at the trigger with no uncertainty or smoothing in the decision boundary.
plan.scientific_mechanism: In practice, surveillance noise, reporting aggregation, and decentralized implementation make activation probabilistic or smoothed across a narrow prevalence band around the nominal trigger.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to change the activation assumption rather than add a new process: the program is still prevalence-triggered and still suppresses contacts by a bounded fraction, but the onset should be rounded near the trigger instead of perfectly discontinuous. The parent target mapping uses a single hard threshold: varying p while holding c0, rho, and p_trigger fixed gives c_eff=c0 for all p<p_trigger and then an immediate departure once p reaches p_trigger. The child would instead produce a smooth threshold surface in the existing input space, so small positive and negative deviations of p around p_trigger already change c_eff. This is an observable change in the scored static mapping itself, not only in an auxiliary trajectory. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce both exact zero suppression just below threshold and partial suppression in that same near-threshold region, because the Heaviside branch structure forbids any below-trigger response. The contrast is scientifically admissible when sampled prevalence values resolve a band around p_trigger; if all observations sit far below or far above the trigger, the refinement is weakly identifiable, which should be stated rather than hidden.

diagnostic_groups.role: coordinate for testing whether equal relative exceedance implies equal suppression

contract.activation_condition: Observable when comparing policies with different admissible p_trigger values and prevalence spanning from low to moderate absolute levels near and above the trigger; especially when p_trigger is small enough that the same relative exceedance can occur at materially different absolute p.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, near-trigger cases already show smoothed activation; in holdout, comparing equal p/p_trigger across wider absolute prevalence values reveals that the activation sharpness and effective suppression are not identical once absolute prevalence differs.
contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when any absolute-prevalence modulation vanishes, so suppression depends only on (p-p_trigger)/p_trigger.
contract.domain_mechanism: Absolute prevalence modulates the strength of a prevalence-triggered intervention response.
contract.scientific_mechanism: Public and programmatic response can be more decisive when absolute prevalence is plainly high, because case visibility, institutional pressure, and individual risk perception depend on absolute burden as well as whether a nominal trigger has been crossed.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the mapping no longer collapses to a single relative-exceedance coordinate; the extra saturation factor changes the geometry of equal-response contours in the observed input plane.
contract.assumption_before: Intervention escalation depends only on normalized exceedance above the trigger.
contract.assumption_after: Intervention escalation remains trigger-based but is additionally modulated by absolute prevalence through a saturating burden-sensitive factor.
contract.before_fragment: c0*(1 - rho*(1 - exp(-(p - p_trigger)/p_trigger - ((p - p_trigger)/p_trigger)**3))*(1 + tanh((p - p_trigger)/p_trigger))/2)
contract.after_fragment: c0*(1 - rho*(1 - exp(-p/p_trigger)*exp(-(p - p_trigger)/p_trigger - ((p - p_trigger)/p_trigger)**3))*(1 + tanh((p - p_trigger)/p_trigger))/2)
contract.parent_reduction: The parent is recovered when exp(-p/p_trigger) is effectively 1, i.e. when the added absolute-prevalence modulation is removed.
contract.observable_signature: Compare cases with equal p/p_trigger but different absolute p, while holding c0 and rho fixed: the parent predicts identical suppression because it depends only on (p-p_trigger)/p_trigger, whereas the child predicts lower c_eff at larger absolute p through the extra exp(-p/p_trigger) damping of the active-regime residue.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this contrast because its target mapping is exactly a one-dimensional function of the relative-excess coordinate once c0 and rho are fixed. Refitting rho or reshaping the existing threshold terms only changes that shared one-dimensional curve; it cannot assign different c_eff values to two observations that share the same p/p_trigger but differ in absolute p.
